title: LASCon: Loop-Aware Scratchpad Condensation for Terminal Agents

contributions.purpose: Solves context-window overflow and unproductive action loops in long-horizon terminal agent tasks without fine-tuning.
contributions.mechanism: LASCon, a training-free scaffold combining a Deterministic CLI Condenser (rule-based extraction preserving commands, exit codes, error lines, truncated outputs, with full logs offloaded to disk) with a Progress-Conditioned Loop Controller that blocks specific repeated actions to force exploration.
contributions.evaluation: On Terminal-Bench 2.0 with Qwen3-32B, LASCon achieves 68.8% completion rate, +21.2 percentage points over the OpenHands default baseline (47.5%), while eliminating all timeout failures (0 vs 36).
contributions.source_quote: LASCon: A training-free scaffold combining deterministic CLI condensation with progress-conditioned loop control, deployable with any LLM backend without fine-tuning.

contributions.purpose: Establishes that deterministic condensation beats LLM-based summarization for CLI contexts.
contributions.mechanism: Ablation study running the Deterministic CLI Condenser (DCC) module alone, without the loop controller.
contributions.evaluation: DCC alone achieves 70.0% completion (+18.8pp over baseline), demonstrating structured context management is the primary driver of improvement.
contributions.source_quote: Empirical finding: Structured context management through DCC alone achieves 70.0% completion (+18.8pp), demonstrating that deterministic condensation outperforms LLM summarization for CLI contexts.

contributions.purpose: Characterizes the actual role of loop control in terminal agent performance.
contributions.mechanism: Analysis of loop-induced failure frequency and Progress-Conditioned Loop Controller (PLC) block-rate/deadlock behavior.
contributions.evaluation: Loop-induced failures are rare (2.5% in baseline) and eliminated by prompting alone; PLC maintains a conservative 0.12% block rate with zero deadlock events, acting as a safety net rather than a primary improvement mechanism.
contributions.source_quote: Analysis: Loop-induced failures are rare (2.5% in baseline) and eliminated by prompting alone; PLC serves as a conservative safety net (0.12% block rate) rather than a primary improvement mechanism.

self_declared_provenance.quote: Unlike these approaches that rely on learned or LLM-based compression, our DCC uses deterministic rules tailored to CLI output structure.

Recent work by Lindenbauer et al. (2025) demonstrates that simple observation masking can match LLM-based summarization for agent context management, suggesting that deterministic approaches may be underexplored.

Our scratchpad mechanism draws inspiration from these memory systems, maintaining structured state information (goal, working directory, recent commands) that supports both context management and loop detection.
The Deterministic CLI Condenser (DCC) replaces LLM-based summarization with rule-based extraction tailored to CLI outputs.

notes: Positive-result paper, but ablation shows DCC alone (70.0%) outperforms the full LASCon system (68.8%), and the second module (PLC) contributes no measurable gain; loop-induced failures were already rare in baseline. Paper carries an automated-research-system generation warning.
